claims.text: Refining refractory high-entropy alloys to a nanocrystalline grain structure increases yield strength relative to coarse-grained or bulk material.
Refining refractory high-entropy alloys to a nanocrystalline grain structure improves ductility relative to coarse-grained or bulk material.
Nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloys can preserve thermal stability.
Nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloys can preserve irradiation stability.
Severe plastic deformation can be used to produce the proposed nanocrystalline structure in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The proposed benefits should hold at temperatures of at least 900 °C and up to approximately 1100 °C.
The proposed nanocrystalline alloy should tolerate helium irradiation representative of reactor or other extreme-environment applications.
A nanocrystalline grain structure provides an increased density of grain boundaries that remain stable under the relevant exposures.
The grain boundaries act as sinks for irradiation-induced point defects.
The grain boundaries act as sinks for dislocations.
Hall–Petch strengthening from the nanocrystalline structure raises yield strength.
Grain-boundary-mediated deformation enhances ductility in the nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloy.
Stable grain boundaries absorb and annihilate irradiation-induced defects.
Nanocrystalline WTaCrVHf exhibits low irradiation-induced defect generation and evolution.
Nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloys can show no detectable grain growth under irradiation.
Nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy-alloy films can remain stable after exposure at 1100 °C for 72 hours.
The nanocrystalline alloy will undergo minimal mechanical-performance degradation under combined elevated-temperature and irradiation exposure.
Excessive thermal exposure or irradiation that causes grain coarsening would negate the mechanical benefits.
